entries.description: Countersigned the orchestrator-drafted E5-quater slots WITH an amendment: the route's constructor checklist (sums, products, composition, exp, log, division) describes a different inductive type. EMLTree is const|var|eml with no division constructor. Walking that checklist would have burned session 1 discovering the type. Caught by checking the source before ratifying — which is what makes a countersignature worth more than a rubber stamp.

Ran the adversarial pass before the proof attempt, per the pre-registration. It succeeded in the first hour. The instruction to try building the counterexample first — not my idea, the drafter's — is what turned four budgeted sessions into one.

Was about to prove 1 < exp(exp a) from scratch; the reachable-lemma index found it already proved 4400 lines up in the same file, since Phase 3. Shipped the citation rather than a duplicate. First time the index prevented redundant work rather than broken work.

Halted rather than pursuing the general floor, on the pre-registered halt point, having chased it exactly far enough to see it reduce to the original problem. No error existed; the chase was going somewhere. The slot written before the session is what made one session the cost instead of three.

Closed the arm with a write-up instead of opening a seventh target. Four of six sessions produced findings by the same move (check the destination exists first); a seventh application would have been pattern-matching, and the arm's results were spread across six commit messages with no single readable statement of what it established.

findings.description: EXIT 3: e/x is an EML tree (eml(eml(const 0, var), const 1)), proved exactly. Decays to 0, never 0 — the lower-bound target is false by construction in session 1. Reframes rather than kills: EventuallyKOverX K is reachable for K = exp(exp a) > 1 always, so K=1 sits below the reachable floor. That is why the framework's lemma is stated for K=1 specifically.

Constant floor localised: 1 < exp(exp a) is the floor theorem, and it was already proved as one_lt_exp_exp_local since Phase 3. The difficulty in 1/x notin EML is that 1 sits BELOW the reachable constant floor, not that 1/x is hard to approximate.

HALT POINT FIRED: the general floor requires deciding whether any EML tree evaluates to a constant multiple of x — the original hard problem. Cost of discovery: one session, which is what the halt point was for. Branch result survives: K<=1 needs exp a = log K <= 0, impossible.
